articles.title: Former world No 1 Jon Rahm quits LIV before breakaway golf series’ relaunch
articles.summary: Two-time major winner is reportedly owed over £100m. Tour filed for bankruptcy after Saudi funding withdrawn. Jon Rahm is to quit LIV Golf due to the “unacceptable” terms offered for the proposed relaunch of the breakaway series.
body: LIV is going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the US after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew support at the end of the season having spent $5bn (£3.7bn) in four years.

While Sergio Garcia and others were successful in petitioning the court to lift the automatic stay on their contracts, in effect freeing them up to pursue other opportunities next year, Rahm was not afforded the same escape.
The Spaniard is one of LIV’s two biggest names – Bryson DeChambeau the other – and is reported to be owed up to $150m (£113m) for the remainder of the contract he signed almost three years ago.

“Mr Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 … and has determined that those terms are unacceptable to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0,” the former world No1’s attorney, John Beck, told a bankruptcy hearing. The Athletic also reported Beck told the court Rahm and LIV are working to finalise a separation agreement by 15 October.
points: Two-time major winner is reportedly owed over £100m.

articles.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery | Marcela Mora y Araujo
articles.summary: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week. “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of…
body: Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team, she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote.

Much was made of Messi’s silence at the time. Then again, much has been made of his visible discomfort with words throughout his epic career. Journalist John Carlin once said that having interviewed Messi twice, he would decline a third opportunity, such was the challenge of getting the little giant to say anything of consequence. In 2010, Juan Sebastián Verón said he had never seen Messi as nervous as when he had to address his teammates for the first time as Argentina captain. In terms of public speaking, perhaps Messi’s most famous outburst was at the 2022 World Cup when he told a Dutch player to “go away”.

articles.title: Is it too early to look at Premier League table?
articles.summary: Just five games in, it might seem a bit early to pay much attention to the Premier League table - but it's probably more settled than you think. BBC Sport takes a look at the statistics behind the early season standings.
body: While it would be no surprise if Manchester City and Arsenal finish as the top two -outside of any points deductions or sanctions directed City's way - will Brentford really qualify for Europe, Hull stay up and Tottenham be involved in yet another relegation battle? Recent history certainly suggests it's likely.
It has to be mentioned there is a huge asterisk hanging over the Premier League table at the moment after Man City were found guilty of the majority of the Premier League charges levelled at them.

The Premier League leaders have appealed but, if the guilty verdict remains, potential sanctions could have a significant impact on the table. Until then, we can only deal with the table as it is now.

If we look at the Premier League after five games last season and where teams ultimately ended up, the final table was already starting to take shape as 13 of the 20 sides finished within four places of where they sat even at this early stage (65%).

articles.title: Verstappen’s victory in Sepang should serve as a warning to Red Bull’s rivals | Giles Richards
articles.summary: Improvements to the car are paying off as the team look to lay the groundwork for renewed success next season. The importance for Max Verstappen of emerging triumphant from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was writ large in the Dutchman’s pleasure at finally being able to drive a competitive car.
body: The transformation was so marked because for so long this season the car has been a handful – the reason Verstappen’s title hopes faded long ago. That the team have come back to deliver a win in such emphatic fashion was no little achievement.

In the opening period of the season, the RB22 was nowhere, deficient in almost every department. It lacked pace, balance, even consistency, and for all his skill Verstappen seemed powerless. He described it as feeling like a passenger in the car at times.

The four-time world champion wrestled it to a couple of podiums in the first half of the season but it was a sisyphean task. “At the start of the season, I really had weekends where I would turn the steering wheel and strange things would happen,” he said. Which, a rather understated critique, belies the fact that the last place a driver wants to be is in a car where he is unsure which way it is going to jump.

articles.title: Compulsory media duties like something in an autocracy - Venter
articles.summary: Saracens' Brendan Venter compares Prem Rugby's media obligations to "something from an autocratic land" after reluctantly speaking at a press conference.
body: Saracens' Brendan Venter compared Prem Rugby's media obligations to "something from an autocratic land" after he made a reluctant appearance at a press conference.
The 56-year-old returned to a full-time role at the club in the summer, initially as director of rugby, but has since been given an updated job title of head of culture and technical director.
His no-show at a pre-season media event cost Saracens a £5,000 fine and he avoided questions before and after the club's opening-round win over Leicester.

However, he appeared alongside head coach Joe Shaw to preview this Saturday's match against Bristol and, after initially offering only short answers to reporters' questions, railed against the expectation that he would be the public face of the club.

articles.title: Two icons, a glorious farewell and a potentially bitter ending
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi's international career ends in fond farewell, Cristiano Ronaldo's is at risk of petering out. BBC Sport takes a look at what could be the end of the international career's of two football greats.
body: On a night where one football legend received a grand farewell from his country, about 6,000 miles away, another released a lengthy statement discussing all the ways in which he had been wronged by his national team coach.
Argentina great Lionel Messi took the adulation of the crowd in Buenos Aires as his glittering international career ended with a goal against Benin on an emotional night.

Meanwhile, Portugal star Cristiano Ronaldo released a statement on social media, accusing manager Jorge Jesus of an "absolute breach of trust" while admitting he should be held accountable for his own actions.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward left his country's Nations League camp last week after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark.

articles.title: Kevin Zeitler takes starting right guard reps for Packers on Wednesday
articles.summary: Last Sunday, Travis Glover did an admirable job filling in as the Green Bay Packers’ right guard in the team’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The offensive line as a whole looked more cohesive than it had through the first three weeks of the season with Glover and veteran acquisition Laken…
body: Heading towards the Packers’ Week 5 matchup with the Chicago Bears, however, it appears that another veteran is preparing to start at right guard. On Wednesday, Kevin Zeitler lined up in that position with the Packers’ number one offensive line unit, a clear signal that the team expects him to be the starter on Sunday afternoon. This tracks with Matt LaFleur’s comments after his signing, when the head coach said “ as soon as (Zeitler) feels good and ready to go, he’ll be in there ” as the starter.

Zeitler starting against the Buccaneers would have been a particularly big ask of a player who is both fresh off the street and recently finished rehab on a quad injury. Not only did he only sign last Wednesday, limiting the time he had to pick up the Packers’ playbook, but the game was taking place in extremely warm weather and on the road. All of the cards were stacked against him playing last week, but those factors are now all gone.

articles.title: Are SPFL away ticket prices too expensive? And is price cap on agenda?
articles.summary: Scotland's top flight is the best attended in Europe per head of population. But does the rising cost of going to games put that status at risk?
body: An adult Kilmarnock supporter heading to Ibrox on Saturday will be asked to hand over £34 to watch their team.
Hibernian fans eager to be at their new manager's debut match at Tannadice will have to part with £30. Dundee punters at Falkirk will have to pay £28, as will St Mirren followers at Tynecastle.
All that before you factor in travel, food and whatever else comes with a day at the football.

Further down the SPFL, the entry fee drops. But Morton fans could still pay £24 at Arbroath in the Championship; Hamilton supporters £21 at Alloa in League 1; and Kelty Hearts followers £18 at Stirling Albion in League 2.

articles.title: Why Sprint in Singapore adds new twist to F1's toughest race
articles.summary: Formula 1 stages its sixth and final Sprint event of the year this weekend to conclude the first flyaway triple header of the sport's busy 2026 season run in.
body: And, for the first time, the Sprint format is being used at the Singapore Grand Prix and its Marina Bay street track, home of the sport's original night race.
But on a track not known for its overtaking, what kind of weekend can we expect with two qualifying sessions and two races?

When the Sprint format was first introduced at three races for the 2021 season, the tracks selected - Silverstone, Monza and Interlagos - were ones deemed to be particularly good for racing so to justify the addition of a 100km race on the Saturday as an appetiser to the main Sunday Grand Prix.
That has generally continued to be the case in the selection of Sprint venues up to this year, with perhaps the inclusion of Imola in 2022 the surprise exception.

articles.title: “I Don’t Accept That”: Dan Campbell Refuses to Accept Lions’ “Mediocre” Football Amid 2-2 Start
articles.summary: Unwilling to accept a return to mediocrity after scraping by the New Orleans Saints (31-30), surviving a winless New York Jets team (31-24), and being defeated by a struggling Carolina Panthers (26-32), Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell is demanding more from his team.
body: Following the loss to the Panthers (2-2) that brought the Lions to 2-2, Campbell appeared on “97.1 The Ticket” on Tuesday morning to say that they will be back on track before the season unravels.

“We’re going to give some other guys an opportunity, and go, man,” Campbell said. “But we’re not going to accept mediocrity. That’s not what we’re doing here,” he said. “We’ve got too many guys playing at a high level, and we’re going to raise the floor on this team.”

“Man, if you want to be great, they should want to score 35 points a game at a minimum,” he said. “That’s what greatness is. That’s what they’re charged with. We got plenty of weapons on offense and if we’re going to accept mediocrity, then, no. Then, yeah, we can make all the excuses in the world. But if we want to spit and sputter and be average, that’s one thing. We’re not going to be average. We’re going to raise the raise the floor on these guys, man. We’re going to push them.”
Campbell denied that finishing 9-8 or 8-9 is the acceptable benchmark for the Lions.
